html:
The capital of Ukraine, on the hills above the Dnieper River, and the first capital of the medieval state of Rus'.

Legend says it was founded by Kyi, a prince of the Polianians, a Slavic tribe. In 882 Prince Oleg, of Scandinavian origin, made it the capital of Kievan Rus'. It sat on the river road from the Baltic to the Black Sea and traded with Constantinople. Around 988 Vladimir the Great had its people baptised in the Dnieper, and his son Yaroslav the Wise built the Cathedral of Saint Sophia. Monks founded the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra in caves nearby. In the 1000s it was one of the largest cities in Europe.

As Rus' split up, Kyiv became the seat of a smaller principality. The Mongols sacked it in 1240. It then passed to Lithuania and Poland, and in the 1600s to the Cossack state and Russia.

In 1918 it was briefly the capital of an independent Ukraine, and from 1934 of Soviet Ukraine. Nazi Germany occupied it in the Second World War and murdered over 33,000 Jews at Babyn Yar in two days in 1941. Since 1991 it has been the capital of independent Ukraine. Mass protests on its Maidan square in 2013 and 2014 toppled a pro-Russian president, and in 2022 its defenders turned back a Russian attack on the city (Russia invades Ukraine).
sum: The capital of Ukraine, on the hills above the Dnieper River, and the first capital of the medieval state of Rus'.
